column2: 中古英语 sobben，或出中古低地德语 sabben（流涎）
column3: to cry with short catches of breath
column5: She sobbed quietly into her sleeve.|A sob broke the long silence.
column6: crying that catches the breath in bursts – 哭时气息一顿一顿地断开
column7: 抽泣：一抽一抽地低声哭|呜咽：低而断续的哭声

column2: 中古英语 sober ← 古法语 sobre ← 拉丁语 sōbrius，由 se-（无）＋ ebrius（醉）构成
column3: not affected by alcohol, or serious in manner
column5: He stayed sober all evening.|She gave a sober assessment of the risk.
column6: without drink and therefore steady – 不带酒意因而稳得住
column7: 未醉的：没有受酒影响|冷静的：不激动而能持平判断

column2: 英式英语，为 association football 的缩略——assoc. 加牛津式后缀 -er 而成，1888 年见于记载
column3: a game played by two teams kicking a round ball
column5: They play soccer every Sunday morning.|Soccer draws the largest crowds here.
column6: the kicking game played under association rules – 按协会规则踢的那种球赛

column2: 古英语 socc（轻便鞋），由日耳曼语支借自拉丁语 soccus ← 希腊语 sykchos（一种鞋）
column3: a knitted covering for the foot worn inside a shoe
column5: He pulled on a pair of wool socks.|One sock had a hole in it.
column6: the soft covering drawn over the foot – 套在脚上的软质织物
column7: 短袜：长度到踝或小腿的袜|袜子：泛指套在脚上的织物

column2: 借自意大利语 soda
column3: a fizzy drink, or a sodium compound used in cleaning
column5: She ordered a glass of soda.|Add baking soda to the mixture.
column6: the bubbling water and the salt that makes it – 起泡的水以及产生它的那种碱盐
column7: 苏打水：含气泡的饮料|苏打：碳酸钠一类的化合物

column2: 借自法语 sofa，更早出阿拉伯语 ṣuffa（铺了毯垫的石砌长座）
column3: a long soft seat for two or more people
column5: They sat together on the old sofa.|The sofa takes up half the room.
column6: a long cushioned seat for several people – 供数人同坐的加垫长座

column2: 古英语 sōfte（原作 sēfte）← 原始西日耳曼语 *samftī（平、缓、柔）← 原始印欧语 *sem-（一、整）
column3: yielding easily to pressure, or gentle
column5: The cushion feels very soft.|She spoke in a soft voice.
column6: giving way easily instead of resisting – 受压就让、不硬抗
column7: 柔软的：一按就凹不坚硬|轻柔的：力度或声音都很轻

column2: 由 soft ＋ -ware 构成，与 hardware 相对，1958 年由 John Tukey 造出
column3: the programs that tell a computer what to do
column5: The software updates itself each night.|They wrote the software in six months.
column6: the instructions as against the machine itself – 相对机器本身而言的那套指令

column2: 中古英语 soile，部分出盎格鲁诺曼语 soyl ← 拉丁语 solium（座）被误认作 solum（地面）；部分出古英语 sol（泥）
column3: the top layer of earth in which plants grow
column5: Rich soil covers the valley floor.|Test the soil before planting.
column6: the layer of ground that plants root in – 供植物扎根的那层地面
column7: 土壤：地表可供耕种的一层|耕土：经耕作的表层土

column2: 中古英语 soudeour ← 古法语 soudier（雇兵）← 中世纪拉丁语 soldarius，源自晚期拉丁语 solidus（一种钱币）——即受饷者
column3: a member of an army
column5: The soldier saluted and stepped back.|Two soldiers guarded the gate.
column6: one who serves for pay in an army – 领饷从军的人
column7: 军人：在军队服役的人|战士：参加战斗的成员

column2: 中古英语 solempne ← 古法语 solempne ← 晚期拉丁语 sōlempnis（拉丁语 sollemnis 的变体，庄严的、每年举行的）
column3: formal and serious in manner
column5: The ceremony was slow and solemn.|He made a solemn promise that day.
column6: carried out with formal gravity – 以正式而庄重的方式进行
column7: 庄严的：场面肃穆令人敬重|郑重的：态度认真不轻率

column2: 中古英语 sum body，由 some ＋ body 复合而成
column3: a person whose identity is not stated
column5: Somebody left a note on the door.|Ask somebody who knows the way.
column6: a person taken as unspecified – 不指明是谁的那个人

column2: 中古英语 sum on，由 some ＋ one 复合而成
column3: one person, not named or not known
column5: Someone called while you were out.|I need someone to help here.
column6: one person among many, left unnamed – 众人之中未点名的一个
column7: 有人：存在某个人做了某事|某个人：指某一位而不明说是谁

column2: 中古英语 somþyng ← 古英语 sum þing，由 some ＋ thing 复合而成
column3: a thing that is not named or known
column5: Something fell behind the cupboard.|She wants something warm to drink.
column6: a thing taken as unspecified – 不指明是什么的那个东西
column7: 某物：不点名的一件东西|某事：不点名的一件事情

column2: 中古英语 somtyme，由 some ＋ time 构成
column3: at an unstated point in time
column5: Come and see us sometime next week.|The letter arrived sometime in May.
column6: at a point in time left unfixed – 落在某个未定的时点上
column7: 某时：未指明的某个时候|改天：另择一个日子

column2: 中古英语 sumtymes，由 sometime ＋ -s 构成
column3: on some occasions but not always
column5: Sometimes he walks to work.|The machine sometimes stops without warning.
column6: on scattered occasions rather than all – 只在个别时候而非一直
column7: 有时：偶尔发生|间或：隔一段出现一次

column2: 由 some ＋ where 复合而成
column3: in or to a place that is not named
column5: She left her keys somewhere upstairs.|We should meet somewhere quieter.
column6: at a place left unspecified – 落在某个未点明的地点
column7: 某处：不指明的某个地方|在某地：处在某个未说明的位置

column2: 古英语 sunu ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sunu ← 原始日耳曼语 *sunuz ← 原始印欧语 *suHnús，出 *sewH-（生育）
column3: a male child of a parent
column5: Their eldest son studies abroad now.|He named his son after his father.
column6: the male one born to a parent – 所生的男性子女
column7: 子嗣：所生的男性子女|男性后代：血脉上属下一代的男性

column2: 古英语 sang ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sangu ← 原始日耳曼语 *sangwaz（歌唱）← 原始印欧语 *sengʷʰ-（唱）
column3: a short piece of music with words to be sung
column5: She wrote the song in one evening.|Everyone joined in the last song.
column6: words set to a tune for singing – 配上曲调供人唱的词
column7: 歌曲：可唱的一首乐曲|歌唱：唱这个行为

column2: 古英语 sōna（立即）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sān ← 原始日耳曼语 *sēna
column3: after only a short time
column5: The bus should arrive soon.|He soon realised his mistake.
column6: after only a short interval – 只隔很短一段之后
column7: 不久：过不了多长时间|很快：短时间内就

column2: 1601 年前后始见于英语 ← 中世纪拉丁语 sophisticatus
column3: highly developed and complex, or worldly-wise
column5: The lab uses sophisticated equipment.|She has a sophisticated taste in music.
column6: refined through much working over – 经反复琢磨而变得考究
column7: 精巧的：结构复杂而做得精细|老练的：见识多而不生涩

column2: 古英语 sār（痛、伤）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sair ← 原始日耳曼语 *sairaz
column3: painful when touched or moved
column5: My shoulder felt sore all week.|He had a sore throat by evening.
column6: hurting when pressed – 一碰就痛
column7: 疼痛的：受触即感到痛|发炎的：局部红肿而痛

column2: 古英语 sorg（忧、愁）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sorgu ← 原始日耳曼语 *surgō ← 原始印欧语 *swergʰ-（忧、病）
column3: deep sadness caused by loss
column5: She spoke of her sorrow quietly.|Sorrow filled the small church.
column6: the heavy grief that settles after loss – 失去之后沉下来的深切哀痛
column7: 悲伤：因失去而深感痛苦|哀愁：绵长而低沉的忧伤

column2: 古英语 sāriġ（悲伤的）← 原始西日耳曼语 *sairag ← 原始日耳曼语 *sairagaz，由 sore ＋ -y 构成；与 sorrow 形近义近而并非同源
column3: feeling regret about something one has done
column5: She was sorry about the delay.|I feel sorry for the whole family.
column6: feeling the sting of having done wrong – 因做错而心里发痛
column7: 抱歉的：为自己的过失感到不安|难过的：为某事感到不好受

column2: 中古英语 sort ← 古法语 sorte（类、种）← 拉丁语 sortem，为 sors（签、份、类）的宾格
column3: a group of things sharing a quality, or to arrange into groups
column5: What sort of music do you like.|She sorted the papers by date.
column6: a share of the whole set apart by kind – 按类分出来的一份
column7: 种类：性质相同的一批|分类：按类别把东西分开

column2: 古英语 sāwol ← 原始西日耳曼语 *saiwalu ← 原始日耳曼语 *saiwalō，更早词源未定
column3: the spiritual part of a person believed to live on
column5: They prayed for the souls of the dead.|The music has real soul.
column6: the part held to outlast the body – 被认为在身体之外仍存续的那部分
column7: 灵魂：被认为独立于肉体的精神本体|心魂：内心深处的情感与精神

column2: 「声音」一支 ← 中古英语 soun ← 古法语 son ← 拉丁语 sonus（声）；同形的「健全」另出古英语 sund
column3: what can be heard, or in good condition
column5: A faint sound came from below.|The old bridge is still sound.
column6: what travels to the ear – 传到耳朵里的那个东西
column7: 声音：耳朵能听到的振动|健全的：状况良好没有毛病

column2: 中古英语 soupe ← 古法语 soupe ← 晚期拉丁语 suppa（浸汤的面包）← 原始日耳曼语 *supô
column3: a liquid food made by boiling ingredients in water
column5: She made soup from the leftover bones.|The soup was too hot to drink.
column6: liquid food that bread was once dipped in – 早先用来蘸面包的那种汤汁
column7: 汤：煮出的液体食物|羹汤：较稠的汤食

column2: 古英语 sūr ← 原始西日耳曼语 *sūr ← 原始日耳曼语 *sūraz ← 原始印欧语 *súHros
column3: having a sharp taste like lemon or vinegar
column5: The apples tasted rather sour.|Milk turns sour in warm weather.
column6: sharp on the tongue – 在舌上发出尖锐的刺激
column7: 酸的：味道带酸味|发酸的：因变质而转酸

column2: 中古英语 sours ← 古法语 sorse，为 sordre（涌起）的过去分词 ← 拉丁语 surgere（升起），由 sub（自下）＋ regere（引）构成
column3: the place or thing from which something comes
column5: They traced the river to its source.|Name the source of your figures.
column6: the point where something rises up – 某物涌起来的那一点
column7: 源头：河流或事物开始的地方|来源：某物或某信息的出处
